title: FedEx Korea Joins Local Conservation Efforts to Preserve Bird Habitats
summary: FedEx team members volunteered for habitat cleanups and feeding along the lower reaches of Gongneungcheon Stream to support migratory bird conservation
body_markdown:
**SEOUL, South Korea, November 24, 2026** — Federal Express Corporation (FedEx), one of the world’s largest express transportation companies, collaborated with the Korea Green Foundation to support wintering migratory bird conservation through employee volunteer activities in Paju, Gyeonggi Province.


On November 21, more than 30 FedEx team members and their families joined habitat cleanups and bird feeding along the lower reaches of Gongneungcheon Stream. Guided by ecological experts from the Korea Green Foundation, the volunteers fed species such as greater white-fronted geese and great egrets, and learned about migratory bird ecology and the importance of habitat protection for maintaining a healthy ecosystem.


The lower reaches of Gongneungcheon Stream are home to many wild birds and serve as a key wintering ground for migratory species. To ensure these birds have access to sufficient food and safe habitats to survive the season, ongoing habitat management and biodiversity conservation are essential. Through the Korea Green Foundation’s “Saesaegakgak” bird conservation campaign, FedEx volunteers help protect these ecologically vital wintering habitats, raise public awareness of the campaign, and engage local communities in conservation efforts.


“It is truly heartening to see our team members turn our commitment into action and make a positive impact in our communities,” said Wonbin Park, managing director of FedEx Korea. “We will continue to support local conservation efforts to help build a more sustainable future.”


FedEx Korea continues to support community initiatives focused on environmental sustainability and social support. These efforts include meal-sharing through the Dail Community’s Babfor Sharing Movement, tree planting with the Korea Green Foundation’s “Let’s Bee Forest” campaign, and donation drives with the Beautiful Store to support underprivileged communities.
